thread:
incident-bot: DETECTED unusual error-rate on /v1/auth in eu-west during staged rollout of auth-gateway-v2. Error rate > 6% for 3m, paging oncall.
maya (oncall): I'm on it, looking at dashboards now.
maya (oncall): Tom - can you confirm if the new gateway is receiving malformed upstream tokens? dash shows spike in 401/502 rather than 5xx.
tom (sre): checking logs. On the canary hosts I'm seeing connection resets to token service + 502 from gateway. Sample log:
```
2026-03-17T02:12:04Z auth-gw[host-12]: upstream read error: EOF while proxying to token-svc:443
2026-03-17T02:12:04Z auth-gw[host-12]: returned 502 to client
```
julia (platform): Launching quick health check across the canary pool. If it's token-svc throttling, we should fallback.
ken (prod-eng): Rolling out the FF too fast? We started at 30% in EU this morning.
lisa (support): Support seeing increased customer tickets in EU complaining about "failed to sign in". No major SSO customers on rotation yet.
maya (oncall): Deploy-bot, can you pause the staged release? We need to stop new sessions hitting auth-gateway-v2.
deploy-bot: Staged release pause request received for release-id release-authv2-20260317. Pausing rollouts to 0% for eu-west.
maya (oncall): Confirm pause applied. No new hosts should get the variant now.
tom (sre): Collecting traces, initial hypothesis: new gateway uses longer connection pool timeout causing token-svc connection saturation under short bursts. Token-svc returns 429 then gateway turns into 502s.
julia (platform): Can we flip the feature flag to route to legacy gateway while we investigate? That's less disruptive than full rollback.
ken (prod-eng): We didn't add a direct FF flip for auth-route; I can run immediate rollback of canary if needed. Which do you prefer? quick FF or rollback?
maya (oncall): Flip FF if it's a single config toggle. Ken, if not, proceed rollback. We need customer impact minimized.
ken (prod-eng): I can run the FF kill command now: `infra/ffctl set auth-gateway-v2 false --env=eu-west --force` — rolling out now.

(90s later)

deploy-bot: Feature flag update applied: auth-gateway-v2 -> false in eu-west.
maya (oncall): Monitor error-rate and support queue. Lisa, any change on tickets?
lisa (support): Tickets trending down; a few still reporting failures but volume dropping. CS queue severity lowered from P1 to P2 for affected customers.

(3m later)

tom (sre): Error rate back to baseline ~0.4%. Traces show clients hitting legacy gateway. No further 502 surge.
maya (oncall): Great. We'll keep the FF off and start incident postmortem. Who owns root cause analysis?
julia (platform): Platform will own investigating connection pooling defaults and token-svc capacity in EU.
ken (prod-eng): I'll work on a safer rollout path and add canary health checks that watch upstream 5xx/429 and connection resets.
sarah (cs): Tentative customer notification draft: "We experienced elevated sign-in failures in EU due to an auth gateway rollout. Traffic has been routed back to the previous gateway. We're investigating and will follow up with a timeline and remediation." Want engineering sign-off before sending.
maya (oncall): Fine to send that with note we'll update in 2 hours. Include that service is restored for most customers.

(handoff)
maya (oncall): I'm handing off to Tom (sre) and Julia (platform) for overnight RCA and mitigation. I'll update incident tracker and tag oncall-secondary for morning review. If anything regresses, page me.
tom (sre): Acknowledged. I'll collect heap/conn metrics and series for token-svc + gateway. Will post findings in #incidents.
julia (platform): Acknowledged. We'll also run a soak test against token-svc and add a circuit-breaker if needed.

incident-bot: Incident auto-log created: INC-2026-032 - eu-west auth-gateway rollout -> failover to legacy gateway. Severity: SEV2. Handoff: maya -> tom/julia.
maya (oncall): Closing paging window. Leaving the thread open for logs and postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:"
